primitives.name: Per-Dimensional Token Discretization
primitives.verbatim_quote: Two schemes: (1) Uniform — tokens cover uniformly-spaced intervals of width (max s^i - min s^i)/V (preserves Euclidean distance info; outliers can strand tokens); (2) Quantile — each token accounts for 1/V of empirical data mass (all tokens represented).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'s^i': 'i-th state dimension, dimensionless', 'V': 'number of discrete tokens per dimension, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Trajectory data can be projected onto a fixed vocabulary of tokens; uniform binning preserves geometric structure while quantile binning ensures full coverage.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Outliers in uniform scheme cause token stranding; quantile scheme fails when data distribution is highly skewed or sparse.

layer2.mapping: Maps continuous state-action space into discrete token sequences suitable for autoregressive modeling.
layer2.telemetry: Log-likelihood improvement over uniform discretization on held-out trajectories.

primitives.name: Trajectory Transformer Decoder
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Model: GPT-style transformer decoder, 4 layers, 4 heads (small vs LLM scale); trained with standard teacher forcing, maximizing Σ log P_θ(token | prefix).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'x_t': 'token at time t, discrete', 'x_{<t}': 'sequence of tokens up to time t, discrete', 'P_\\theta': 'autoregressive probability model parameterized by θ, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Trajectory distribution admits fixed-vocabulary autoregressive representation; training via teacher forcing is sufficient for convergence.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure under high-dimensional or non-stationary state spaces where token dependencies exceed model capacity.

layer2.telemetry: Normalized return performance on D4RL locomotion tasks.

primitives.name: Reward-Biased Beam Search Planner
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Planning = decoding: beam search (Algorithm 1) over token sequences, modified to bias beams by cumulative predicted reward; variations yield imitation learning (unbiased sampling), goal-reaching (condition on goal), and offline RL (reward-biased search).

primitives.assumptions: Planning via beam search approximates optimal policy under reward bias; reward function is known or estimable.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degenerates in high-reward variance settings or when reward signal is sparse or misleading.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that offline reinforcement learning can be reframed as a sequence modeling problem by treating trajectories as unstructured token sequences. Each (state, action, reward) tuple becomes a token, and the model learns to predict the next token given previous ones. This allows leveraging powerful language modeling techniques such as GPT-style transformers. The discretization step maps continuous variables into a fixed vocabulary, which is critical for tractability. Uniform discretization preserves Euclidean distances but may misrepresent outliers; quantile discretization ensures even coverage but may lose local structure. The transformer decoder then models the conditional probability of future tokens, enabling long-horizon predictions. Beam search planning introduces reward bias during decoding to guide exploration towards high-value outcomes, effectively replacing traditional policy optimization. Joint modeling of state and action inherently discourages out-of-distribution actions, eliminating the need for explicit pessimism. This framework supports both prediction and control within a unified architecture.
